categories.main_business_segments: Expedia Group operates through three main business segments: Retail, B2B, and trivago. The Retail segment includes consumer-facing travel brands such as Expedia.com, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, and others, offering a wide range of travel and advertising services. The B2B segment encompasses Expedia Partner Solutions, which provides travel services to third-party businesses, and previously included Egencia, a corporate travel management company (sold in 2021). The trivago segment operates a hotel metasearch platform generating advertising revenue by referring users to travel service providers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Expedia leverages proprietary technology platforms, unified data engineering, and scalable cloud infrastructure to connect travelers with suppliers and manage bookings. The company utilizes APIs, white-label solutions, and agent tools for partners, and has invested in AI-driven customer service, virtual agent platforms, and a multi-year migration to public cloud services (e.g., AWS). Its systems support 24/7 global operations, dynamic packaging, and loyalty programs, with ongoing enhancements to improve efficiency and traveler experience.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Expedia serves both leisure and business travelers globally through its consumer brands, as well as travel suppliers (hotels, airlines, property owners) and business partners (corporate travel managers, travel agents, financial institutions) via its B2B offerings. Key end markets include lodging (hotels and alternative accommodations), air travel, car rentals, cruises, and travel insurance, with a significant focus on both individual consumers and enterprise partners.
categories.geographic_coverage: Expedia operates worldwide, with localized websites and services in numerous countries across North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. The United States is its largest market, but the company maintains a significant presence in Europe (notably through trivago and Hotels.com), Australia, Canada, and other international regions. Its supply portfolio and customer base are global, with offices and employees in over 50 countries.
categories.supply_chain_position: Expedia functions primarily as an intermediary (midstream) in the travel supply chain, connecting travelers with suppliers such as hotels, airlines, and property owners. It does not own travel inventory but facilitates bookings and transactions between suppliers and end customers, earning commissions, fees, or margins on these services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Expedia's strategic focus is on leveraging its platform and brand strength to drive innovation, improve traveler experiences, and achieve profitable growth. Key initiatives include unifying technology and loyalty programs across brands, enhancing AI and data-driven personalization, expanding alternative accommodations, and streamlining operations for efficiency. The company is also investing in cloud migration, customer service automation, and expanding its B2B partnerships.
categories.revenue_model: Expedia generates revenue through three primary models: the merchant model (Expedia is the merchant of record and earns the margin between supplier cost and traveler payment), the agency model (Expedia earns commissions or fees for facilitating bookings), and the advertising model (revenue from advertising placements and referrals, primarily via trivago and Expedia Media Solutions). In 2021, merchant, agency, and advertising/media/other accounted for 64%, 27%, and 9% of total revenue, respectively.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Expedia faces intense competition from global online travel agencies (OTAs) such as Booking Holdings (Booking.com, Agoda), Trip.com, and Airbnb, as well as from travel suppliers' direct channels, metasearch engines (e.g., Kayak, TripAdvisor), and search engines like Google. Expedia is one of the largest OTAs globally, with a broad brand portfolio and significant international reach, but operates in a highly competitive and consolidating industry.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, Expedia reported $8.6 billion in revenue, up 65% from 2020 but still below pre-pandemic levels ($12.1 billion in 2019), reflecting ongoing recovery from COVID-19 impacts. Gross bookings were $72.4 billion in 2021, with positive operating income ($186 million) after a significant loss in 2020. The company has a large global scale, significant liquidity ($4.3 billion in cash and investments at year-end 2021), and is focused on returning to sustained growth and profitability.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Expedia emphasizes its comprehensive, multi-brand travel platform, offering travelers a broad selection of lodging, flights, car rentals, and experiences, as well as flexible booking options and a unified loyalty program. Its value proposition includes global reach, technology-driven convenience, competitive pricing, and the ability to bundle travel products. For suppliers and partners, Expedia provides access to a large global audience, advanced merchandising tools, and data-driven insights to drive demand and revenue.
